rules.reason: Australian Consumer Law section 18 prohibits misleading or deceptive conduct, or conduct likely to mislead or deceive, in trade or commerce.
rules.correction: Remove or qualify any misleading overall impression and verify material product representations against evidence.

rules.reason: ACCC guidance says advertising claims should be accurate, based on reasonable grounds, and capable of proof, including claims conveyed through images and social media.
rules.correction: Retain evidence for objective claims or replace them with accurate, supportable product facts.

rules.reason: New Zealand's Fair Trading Act prohibits misleading or deceptive conduct and false or misleading representations in trade.
rules.correction: Remove misleading representations and check the advertisement's overall impression against current product evidence.

rules.reason: New Zealand Commerce Commission guidance requires a reasonable basis for express and implied product or service representations when they are made.
rules.correction: Hold a reasonable evidential basis before making the representation, or remove the claim.

rules.reason: The UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 framework prohibits misleading actions and omissions likely to cause an average consumer to take a different transactional decision.
rules.correction: Correct misleading information, disclose material information clearly, and reassess the overall impression for the average consumer.

rules.reason: CAP Code section 3 requires non-broadcast marketing communications not to materially mislead and requires documentary evidence for objective claims capable of substantiation.
rules.correction: Hold documentary evidence before publication, qualify material limitations clearly, or remove the objective claim.

rules.reason: FTC truth-in-advertising requirements call for advertising claims to be truthful, non-deceptive, fair and evidence-based.
rules.correction: Correct deceptive or unfair impressions and retain appropriate evidence for objective claims before dissemination.

rules.reason: FTC policy requires a reasonable basis for express and implied objective claims before an advertisement is disseminated.
rules.correction: Possess the represented or otherwise reasonable level of substantiation before publishing the claim, or remove it.

rules.reason: Copyright Act 1968, Compilation No. 65, is the Australian copyright statute in force on 2 April 2026. An advertisement that reproduces someone else's work needs a permission or an exception the Act provides.
rules.correction: Remove material the advertiser does not have a right to reproduce, or keep the permission with the campaign record.

rules.reason: The AANA Code of Ethics, effective 1 February 2021, requires advertising to be legal, honest and truthful, and sets the consumer-complaint rules on portrayal, violence, sex, language, health, safety and distinguishability.
rules.correction: Change the advertisement so it meets the Code section the complaint would rely on, or do not publish it.

rules.reason: The brand policy is the retailer profile saved in this workspace: tone, visual style, approved terms and banned terms. It is read at review time and is not a separate statute.
rules.correction: Remove any banned term and keep the advertisement inside the saved tone and approved terms.

rules.reason: The AANA Code applies to online and social media the advertiser controls, including an Instagram post. Meta's own Advertising Standards page did not return extractable policy text, so it is not copied here.
rules.correction: Check the Instagram post against the Code's consumer-complaint section, including the social-media audience note.

rules.reason: The AANA Code defines Medium to include the internet and other direct-to-consumer media, so a website advertisement is within the Code.
rules.correction: Apply the same Code sections to the website advertisement as to any other medium.

rules.reason: Spam Act 2003, Compilation No. 10, regulates commercial electronic messages, including consent and a functional unsubscribe facility.
rules.correction: Do not send the email unless the Spam Act conditions for that message are met, including consent and unsubscribe.
